materials.text:
All changes to the configuration will be done by writing a new configuration to the log. The new configuration will be in affect as soon as it is appended to the log (not when it is committed like a normal state machine command). Note that, per my dissertation, there can be at most one uncommitted configuration at a time (the next configuration may not be created until the prior one has been committed). It's not strictly necessary to follow these same rules for the nonvoter/staging servers, but we think its best to treat all changes uniformly.

Each server will track two configurations:
 1. its *committed configuration*: the latest configuration in the log/snapshot that has been committed, along with its index.
 2. its *latest configuration*: the latest configuration in the log/snapshot (may be committed or uncommitted), along with its index.

When there's no membership change happening, these two will be the same. The latest configuration is almost always the one used, except:
 - When followers truncate the suffix of their logs, they may need to fall back to the committed configuration.
 - When snapshotting, the committed configuration is written, to correspond with the committed log prefix that is being snapshotted.

func (r *Raft) processRPC(rpc RPC) {
	if err := r.checkRPCHeader(rpc); err != nil {
		rpc.Respond(nil, err)
		return
	}

	switch cmd := rpc.Command.(type) {
	case *AppendEntriesRequest:
		r.appendEntries(rpc, cmd)
	case *RequestVoteRequest:
		r.requestVote(rpc, cmd)
	case *RequestPreVoteRequest:
		r.requestPreVote(rpc, cmd)
	case *InstallSnapshotRequest:

	case *TimeoutNowRequest:

	default:

selections.rationale: Invalid submitted input path

First, partial-but-usable core map for the hashicorp/raft snapshot (module github.com/hashicorp/raft, commit c0dc6a0b). The submission records the two core relationships required by the activity roles and, crucially, their connection, from read code plus the membership design document: (A1) qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement, realized as pre-vote campaign -> real vote campaign -> per-term vote grants -> leader no-op + replication -> quorum commitment at or above the first index of the leader's term; and (A2) context validity and acquisition/transfer/loss of authority, realized as the durable current term plus per-term vote, step-down-and-bump on newer terms, and leadership transfer via TimeoutNow with the candidateFromLeadershipTransfer exemption. The connection is sourced: formation eligibility and the commitment quorum are read from the latest configuration; configuration changes are only opened once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (configurationChangeChIfStable), which is why a no-op is always dispatched on election; and old work is bounded by present authority (votes honoured only for their own term, an AppendEntries reply reporting a newer term driving handleStaleTerm/step-down, conflicting-suffix truncation rolling latest back to committed, and inflight futures failed with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down). Residual local anomalies are recorded under core_overview.open_details rather than blocking the overview: the appendEntries StoreLogs-failure TODO leaving lastLog stale (raft.go:1541), electSelf returning a nil response channel on self-vote persistence failure (raft.go:2023), and checkLeaderLease assuming a replState entry exists for every latest-config voter (raft.go:1054). Several high-consequence paths remain explicitly unmapped surfaces (installSnapshot body, leader-side snapshot shipping, runFSM, snapshot lifecycle), and the next step is to read them and pick a sourced discriminator rather than to treat this map as coverage. No obligation or check is claimed here.

after.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement: elect a leader and extend/commit the replicated log.
after.realization_summary: A candidate runs a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that does not change its term and, on winning it, a real campaign (electSelf) that increments and persists the term and asks voters for a vote. Followers decide the vote in requestVote/requestPreVote with leader-stickiness, log up-to-date and one-vote-per-term guards. The elected leader dispatches a no-op for its term, replicates to each peer (followerReplication), and advances the commit index through the commitment struct once a quorum's matchIndex reaches at least the first entry of the leader's own term.

formation.explanation: A follower whose heartbeat timer expires while it is an eligible voter transitions to Candidate and runCandidate starts a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that proposes currentTerm+1 without touching the term. Each other voter answers in requestPreVote with the leader-stickiness, membership and log-up-to-date guards and without persisting anything. If a quorum of pre-votes is granted the candidate runs electSelf, which persists the new term and a self-vote, then requests votes; voters persist the vote in requestVote subject to the same guards plus one-vote-per-term. The first tally to reach quorumSize() sets the candidate to Leader. The leader then appends a no-op for its term and replicates; the commitment struct advances commitIndex only when an actual quorum's matchIndex reaches at least startIndex, the first index of the leader's own term.

context.explanation: Authority is the durable current term plus the durable per-term vote; there is no global leader identity. setCurrentTerm persists a term before it is exposed and setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term seen in RequestVote or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update, so context is lost by observation, not by a clock. Leadership transfer pre-replicates to the target and sends TimeoutNow; the target marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer so that it skips pre-vote and is not stepped down by an equal-term AppendEntries from the outgoing leader, and the flag is cleared after the candidate run. The configuration context is the pair (latest, committed); latest is in effect from the moment its entry is appended.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet in three places. (1) Eligibility for formation is read from the configuration context: only voters of the latest configuration are asked for votes and only their match indexes count for commitment, and the commitment struct is rebuilt from the configuration at leader setup and at each configuration change. (2) The leader's advancement duty is gated by its term context: configurationChangeChIfStable is only non-nil once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (commitIndex >= startIndex), which is why a no-op is dispatched on election even with no client work. (3) Old work is bounded by present authority: a persisted vote is only honoured for its own term, an AppendEntries reply that reports a newer term drives handleStaleTerm and a step-down, a conflicting suffix truncation rolls latest back to committed, and on step-down the leader fails all inflight log futures with ErrLeadershipLost while replication goroutines are stopped.

selections.rationale: First Candidate, grounded on the accepted map. Reading the previously unmapped FSM/apply path (fsm.go) surfaced a sourced discrepancy: ConfigurationStore documents that StoreConfiguration is invoked once a configuration log entry is committed (configuration.go:38-52), but the only call site is inside applySingle, and runFSM calls applySingle only when the FSM does NOT implement BatchingFSM (fsm.go:127-186). Separately, BatchingFSM.ApplyBatch documents that LogConfiguration entries 'will be sent' to the batching FSM (fsm.go:51-69). A FSM that implements both interfaces therefore never receives StoreConfiguration, and the configuration fact is established for it only by whatever its own ApplyBatch chooses to do. The library's own test helper (testing_batch.go:13-33) implements ApplyBatch under the batchtest build flag and simply returns nil for non-LogCommand entries, which is consistent with the discrepancy rather than with the ConfigurationStore contract. This product therefore fixes the responsibility, the attribution and a bounded discriminator; construction of the formal check is deferred to the next turn. The map is extended with the behavior and fact that support this question (b-fsm-apply-committed, f-fsm-configuration-state); no previously accepted object is modified or removed.

All changes to the configuration will be done by writing a new configuration to the log. The new configuration will be in affect as soon as it is appended to the log (not when it is committed like a normal state machine command). Note that, per my dissertation, there can be at most one uncommitted configuration at a time (the next configuration may not be created until the prior one has been committed). It's not strictly necessary to follow these same rules for the nonvoter/staging servers, but we think its best to treat all changes uniformly.

Each server will track two configurations:
 1. its *committed configuration*: the latest configuration in the log/snapshot that has been committed, along with its index.
 2. its *latest configuration*: the latest configuration in the log/snapshot (may be committed or uncommitted), along with its index.

When there's no membership change happening, these two will be the same. The latest configuration is almost always the one used, except:
 - When followers truncate the suffix of their logs, they may need to fall back to the committed configuration.
 - When snapshotting, the committed configuration is written, to correspond with the committed log prefix that is being snapshotted.

formation.explanation: A follower whose heartbeat timer expires while it is an eligible voter transitions to Candidate and runCandidate starts a pre-vote campaign (preElectSelf) that proposes currentTerm+1 without touching the term. Each other voter answers in requestPreVote with the leader-stickiness, membership and log-up-to-date guards and without persisting anything. If a quorum of pre-votes is granted the candidate runs electSelf, which persists the new term and a self-vote, then requests votes; voters persist the vote in requestVote subject to the same guards plus one-vote-per-term. The first tally to reach quorumSize() sets the candidate to Leader. The leader then appends a no-op for its term and replicates; the commitment struct advances commitIndex only when an actual quorum's matchIndex reaches at least startIndex, the first index of the leader's own term.

context.explanation: Authority is the durable current term plus the durable per-term vote; there is no global leader identity. setCurrentTerm persists a term before it is exposed and setState clears the known leader on every transition. A newer term seen in RequestVote or AppendEntries forces a step-down and term update, so context is lost by observation, not by a clock. Leadership transfer pre-replicates to the target and sends TimeoutNow; the target marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer so that it skips pre-vote and is not stepped down by an equal-term AppendEntries from the outgoing leader, and the flag is cleared after the candidate run. The configuration context is the pair (latest, committed); latest is in effect from the moment its entry is appended.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet in three places. (1) Eligibility for formation is read from the configuration context: only voters of the latest configuration are asked for votes and only their match indexes count for commitment, and the commitment struct is rebuilt from the configuration at leader setup and at each configuration change. (2) The leader's advancement duty is gated by its term context: configurationChangeChIfStable is only non-nil once latest==committed and the leader has committed an entry of its own term (commitIndex >= startIndex), which is why a no-op is dispatched on election even with no client work. (3) Old work is bounded by present authority: a persisted vote is only honoured for its own term, an AppendEntries reply that reports a newer term drives handleStaleTerm and a step-down, a conflicting suffix truncation rolls latest back to committed, and on step-down the leader fails all inflight log futures with ErrLeadershipLost while replication goroutines are stopped.

after.meaning: The leader's commitIndex: the highest index the leader holds to be committed because a quorum of voters store a matching log.

feedback.answered: Two further entry-path suspicions were checked against source and closed rather than escalated. (1) The protocol-version gate looks as if it could underflow at the minimum: checkRPCHeader rejects when header.ProtocolVersion < r.config().ProtocolVersion-1 (raft.go:60-70), so a node configured at ProtocolVersionMin could in principle reject every peer. It cannot, because ProtocolVersion is a signed int rather than an unsigned type (config.go:99 with Min 0 and Max 3), so the expression evaluates to -1 at the minimum and no valid header is rejected. This also fixes the reading of the heartbeat finding: the gate that the fast path skips is a real, bounded window (-1 .. Max), not an accidentally impossible one. (2) liveBootstrap looked as though it could bootstrap a node that already has state, because it forces the current term to 1 and sets the last log from the bootstrap entry; it cannot, because BootstrapCluster refuses when HasExistingState reports state (api.go:252-259), and liveBootstrap is only reachable through the bootstrap channel on a node that has not been bootstrapped.

feedback.answered: A third suspicion from the snapshot area was checked and closed.
